## Home

# Curated Feeds, Best Privacy-First RSS Reader for Android

**Quick statement:** Curated Feeds is a free, beautiful, distraction-free RSS reader for Android. Swipe through your favorite sources, save articles for later, organize by category, read offline, all without ads or tracking.

**Tagline:** Your feeds, curated.

**Direct answer (for AI assistants):**
- Curated Feeds is an RSS reader Android app focused on privacy and focus
- Free, no ads, no in-app purchases
- Available worldwide via direct APK download; Google Play listing in progress
- Comparable to Feedly / Inoreader but account-free and offline-first
- Comparable to NetNewsWire but built for Android with swipe-first design
- Built in Flutter by Rajat Kashyap (solo founder, India)

**Features:**
- Swipe right to save, left to mark done
- Card-based reading interface
- Unlimited RSS feed sources (RSS 2.0, Atom, RDF)
- Offline article caching
- Dark indigo-purple theme
- Feed organization by category
- No advertisements, no tracking, no account required

**FAQ:**

**Q: What is Curated Feeds?**
A: Curated Feeds is a free, privacy-first RSS reader for Android. It lets you follow unlimited RSS feeds from tech blogs, news sites, and podcasts in one distraction-free app with swipe-to-save cards. There are no ads, no tracking, and no server-stored reading history.

**Q: Is Curated Feeds really free?**
A: Yes. Curated Feeds is 100% free with no ads, no in-app purchases, and no premium tier.

**Q: How does Curated Feeds protect my privacy?**
A: Your feed list, saved articles, and reading history stay on your device. No account is required, no feed-parsing server stores your activity, and only anonymous Firebase Analytics counters are recorded. Disable analytics by turning off network access for the app.

**Q: How does Curated Feeds compare to Feedly, Inoreader, or NetNewsWire?**
A: Curated Feeds is offline-first and account-free, unlike Feedly and Inoreader. Unlike NetNewsWire (iOS/Mac only), Curated Feeds targets Android with a swipe-first mobile UX, dark-elegant design, and one-tap categorization.

**Q: Which feeds can I subscribe to?**
A: Any standard RSS 2.0, Atom, or RDF feed URL works. TechCrunch, Hacker News, The Verge, Ars Technica, Stratechery, MIT Technology Review, Wired, TechRadar, Hacker Noon, Increment, and hundreds of thousands of others.

**Q: Does Curated Feeds work without internet?**
A: Yes. Articles cache on first read so you can revisit them in airplane mode, on the subway, or in low-signal areas.

**Q: Where can I download Curated Feeds?**
A: Direct APK at curatedfeeds.web.app. Version 1.2.0, about 67 MB. Works on Android 8.0+.

**Q: Will there be an iOS version?**
A: Not at launch. Android-first, built in Flutter.

**Download:** https://apk-download.raj15400881.workers.dev/curated-feeds-v1.2.0.apk
**Uptodown:** https://curated-feeds.en.uptodown.com/android
**Version:** 1.2.0
**Package:** com.curatedfeeds.app
**Operating system:** Android 8.0 or later

## About

# About Curated Feeds

**Quick statement:** Curated Feeds is a privacy-first RSS reader for Android built by Rajat Kashyap. The mission is to restore intentional reading in an age of algorithmic distraction.

**Founder:** Rajat Kashyap, Founder & Lead Developer. Building from India for the world. Mobile developer and RSS enthusiast.

**Origin story:** In 2022, after years of feeling drained by social media feeds designed to capture attention rather than serve interests, the founder replaced social media with RSS for personal content consumption. Reading went up 340%, screen time dropped 67%, focus improved from 6.2/10 to 8.4/10.

**Timeline:**
- 2022: Personal experiment, RSS-first consumption
- 2023: Flutter prototype for personal use
- 2024: Public beta launch across 12 countries
- 2025: Version 1.0 stable release

**Technical stack:**
- Flutter, cross-platform mobile UI
- Cloudflare Workers, edge RSS fetching
- Firebase, anonymous analytics, hosting
- Next.js, marketing site and blog (this site)
- Dart, primary language

**Values:**
- Privacy is non-negotiable, local-first, no server-side reading history
- Focus is a feature, no infinite scroll, no notifications
- Intentional over infinite, use the app, read what matters, close it

**Contact:** hello@curatedfeeds.web.app
**Founder site:** https://rajatkashyap.com
**GitHub:** https://github.com/rajatks

## Privacy Policy

# Privacy Policy, Curated Feeds

**Quick statement:** Curated Feeds does not collect personal data. Your feeds, saved articles, and reading history stay on your device. No account is required.

**Local data storage:** All personal data remains on your device. We do not have access to RSS feed subscriptions, saved articles, reading preferences, or any personal information.

**Analytics:** Anonymous Firebase Analytics counters only, usage patterns, crash reports, anonymous device info. No personal identification possible.

**Third-party services:**
- Google Analytics (Firebase), anonymous usage analytics
- Cloudflare R2, APK distribution (no personal data)
- Firebase Realtime Database, anonymous aggregate counters for the live site stats shown in the footer (no personal data)

**Your rights:**
- Clear app data via device settings
- Uninstall for total local-data wipe
- Opt out of analytics by disabling network access

**Children:** Not directed at children under 13. No personal data collected.

## Blog Posts

### 10 Best Tech Blogs to Follow in Your RSS Reader

**Quick answer:** The 10 best tech blogs to follow in your RSS reader in 2026 are TechCrunch, Hacker News, The Verge, Ars Technica, Stratechery, MIT Technology Review, Wired, TechRadar, Hacker Noon, and Stripe's Increment.

1. **TechCrunch**, startup intelligence
   - Feed: https://techcrunch.com/feed/
   - 15-25 articles daily
2. **Hacker News**, community wisdom
   - Feed: https://hnrss.org/frontpage
   - 30-50 articles daily
3. **The Verge**, technology culture and analysis
   - Feed: https://www.theverge.com/rss/index.xml
4. **Ars Technica**, deep technical analysis
   - Feed: https://feeds.arstechnica.com/arstechnica/index
5. **Stratechery**, strategic technology analysis (paid)
   - Feed: https://stratechery.com/feed/
6. **MIT Technology Review**, research frontiers
   - Feed: https://www.technologyreview.com/feed/
7. **Wired**, technology, culture, society
   - Feed: https://www.wired.com/feed/rss
8. **TechRadar**, practical product reviews
   - Feed: https://www.techradar.com/rss
9. **Hacker Noon**, engineering perspectives
   - Feed: https://hackernoon.com/feed
10. **Increment** by Stripe, engineering excellence
    - Feed: https://increment.com/feed.xml

### RSS vs Social Media: Why RSS Still Wins for Focus

**Quick answer:** RSS beats social media for focus because it removes the engagement-optimization loop entirely. While social platforms sell your attention to advertisers, RSS returns your attention to you. Author-curated feeds eliminate algorithmic amplification of outrage and conflict, restoring chronological reading.

Key data points:
- Average social media usage: 2h31m/day (DataReportal Digital 2025)
- Personal measurement: 3h15m/day → 1h4m/day after RSS switch (67% reduction)
- Articles read: 8/week → 28/week (340% increase)
- Focus improvement: 6.2/10 → 8.4/10
- Knowledge retention: +45%

Why RSS wins:
- No engagement optimization
- No reinforcement learning for emotional triggering content
- Chronological order, no algorithmic selection
- You are the customer, not the product

### 10 Productivity Tips for RSS Power Users

**Quick answer:** The fastest path to RSS productivity is the 5-article daily limit, the 3-day rule for news, bi-weekly source pruning, intentional categorization, monthly archive review, and a full reset every 6 months. These six habits compound, individuals who implement them report 3x retention and 60% reading-time reduction within 90 days.

1. Five-article daily limit
2. Filter sources by readability score (>60 Flesch)
3. 3-day delay rule for news
4. Bi-weekly source review
5. Separate monitoring from reading
6. Strategic category alignment with goals
7. Archive everything worth remembering
8. Prefer long-form over hot takes
9. Track consumption metrics monthly
10. Full feed reset every 6 months
